newsitem.title: UK: Stakis hotel occupancy flat, room rates up.
newsitem.headline: Stakis hotel occupancy flat, room rates up.

text.p: Hotel and leisure group Stakis Plc said its hotels, excluding the Metropole, showed an occupancy level of 71.8 percent in the first 13 weeks of 1997, a touch down from 72 percent last time.
But its average room rate rose to 50.10 pounds over the same period, up from 45.58 pounds in 1996.
Occupancy levels were pulled back slightly by the temporary closure of the Stakis Tyneside where work is underway on a 3.5 million pound refurbishment due to be completed in April.

The 327 million pound acquisition of Metropole hotels was completed on November 20 and traded under the Stakis flag for six weeks in the quarter. During the six week period Metropole, with some 2,266 rooms available, showed 64.7 percent occupancy at an average price per room of 64.77 pounds.
Attendance at Stakis' casinos rose to 603,000 in the quarter up from 525,000, but the spend per head fell to 110 pounds from 129 pounds.
Turnover at the company's casinos increased by 20 percent to 14.2 million pounds driven by the 17 percent increase in attendances.
Stakis reported full year results in December which showed a 24 percent increase in pretax profits before exceptionals to 30.7 million pounds for the year to September 29, 1996.
The company owns 50 hotels or about 7,659 bedrooms, 22 casinos, one hotel/casino and seven premier and 21 hotel leisure clubs currently under the LivingWell banner.
